name: Set 7: Durban to Dullstroom
description: Ball Sports, Potjiekos Secrets, 2000s Hits & Mountain Ranges

questions.q: In a standard game of darts, what color is the narrow outer ring that awards double points?
questions.fact: Alternates between red and green on standard London bristle boards.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for table salt?
questions.fact: Sodium chloride (NaCl).

questions.q: How many degrees are there in a full circle?
questions.fact: A complete rotation is 360 degrees.

questions.q: Which South African craft gin botanical gives pink gin its blush tint and floral flavor?
questions.fact: Hibiscus flowers or rose pelargonium impart natural pink hue.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Portugal?
questions.fact: Lisbon, located at the mouth of the Tagus River.

questions.q: How many days are in the month of September?
questions.fact: 'Thirty days hath September, April, June, and November...'

questions.q: In automotive engines, what does 'RPM' stand for?
questions.fact: Measures crankshaft rotational speed.

questions.q: What famous board game challenges players to sink each other's aircraft carriers and submarines on a coordinate grid?
questions.fact: 'You sank my battleship!'

questions.q: Which primary color mixed with red makes orange?
questions.fact: Red + Yellow = Orange.

questions.q: What is the common term in South Africa for a small, enclosed backyard barbecue space with a built-in chimney?
questions.fact: A dedicated braai room or lapa is the social center of any South African home.

questions.q: What was the final score in the 2023 Rugby World Cup Final when South Africa defeated New Zealand in Paris?
questions.fact: Springboks 12 - All Blacks 11 at Stade de France on 28 October 2023.

questions.q: In golf, what is the term for scoring three under par on a single hole (or a hole-in-one on a par 4)?
questions.fact: An albatross is three strokes under par.

questions.q: Which South African cricket captain led the Proteas to the number 1 Test ranking in the world in 2012 by beating England at Lord's?
questions.fact: Graeme Smith captained South Africa to historic series victories in England and Australia.

questions.q: What is the name of the stadium in Bloemfontein that serves as the home ground of the Free State Cheetahs?
questions.fact: Toyota Stadium in Bloemfontein.

questions.q: In rugby union, what is the minimum distance the ball must travel forward from a kickoff restart before it can be played?
questions.fact: The kickoff must cross the receiving team's 10-meter line.

questions.q: Which South African female golfer won the Women's British Open at Sunningdale in 2007?
questions.fact: Ashleigh Buhai later won the Women's Open in 2022 at Muirfield.

questions.q: Which famous Springbok lock was known for his legendary punch during a test match against New Zealand and his ferocious partnership with Victor Matfield?
questions.fact: Bakkies Botha: one of the most physically intimidating enforcers in rugby history.

questions.q: In soccer, what is the name of the prestigious European club tournament won by Real Madrid a record 15 times?
questions.fact: Formerly the European Cup.

questions.q: Which iconic South African lock forward became the most-capped Springbok player of all time in 2024, surpassing Victor Matfield's 127 caps?
questions.fact: Eben Etzebeth won his 128th cap against Argentina in Nelspruit in September 2024.

questions.q: In cricket, what color ball is traditionally used in day-night Test matches played under floodlights?
questions.fact: The pink ball maintains visibility under lights while retaining red-ball durability.

questions.q: Who directed the 1972 mafia masterpiece The Godfather?
questions.fact: Adapted from Mario Puzo's bestselling novel.

questions.q: In the film Forrest Gump, what college football team did Forrest play for under coach Bear Bryant?
questions.fact: 'Run, Forrest, run!' for the University of Alabama.

questions.q: Which actor portrayed the eccentric pirate Captain Jack Sparrow in Pirates of the Caribbean?
questions.fact: Johnny Depp earned an Oscar nomination for The Curse of the Black Pearl.

questions.q: In the 1993 thriller The Fugitive, who played the wrongfully convicted Dr. Richard Kimble?
questions.fact: 'I didn't kill my wife!' / 'I don't care!'

questions.q: Which 1994 prison drama starring Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman is currently the top-rated movie of all time on IMDb?
questions.fact: Based on a Stephen King novella.

questions.q: In The Lord of the Rings, what is the fictional volcanic mountain in Mordor where the One Ring was forged?
questions.fact: Where Frodo Baggins must cast the Ring into the fires.

questions.q: Who played the eccentric British detective Sherlock Holmes in Guy Ritchie's 2009 action-mystery film?
questions.fact: Robert Downey Jr. won a Golden Globe for the performance.

questions.q: In the hit comedy Anchorman, what is the full name of Will Ferrell's mustachioed 1970s news anchor?
questions.fact: 'Stay classy, San Diego.'

questions.q: Which 1986 film starred Tom Cruise as naval aviator Maverick and featured Kenny Loggins' hit 'Danger Zone'?
questions.fact: Directed by Tony Scott.

questions.q: Which South African actor played the brutal villain Sharlto Copley's sidekick or featured as Wikus van de Merwe in District 9 (2009)?
questions.fact: Sharlto Copley starred as Wikus van de Merwe in Neill Blomkamp's breakout sci-fi hit.

questions.q: What material is a traditional three-legged South African potjie pot made of?
questions.fact: Heavy cast iron retains and distributes gentle, even heat.

questions.q: What is the process called of treating a new or rusty cast iron potjie pot with oil and heat to build a non-stick protective patina?
questions.fact: Coating with fat or oil and baking it creates a polymerized protective layer.

questions.q: What popular South African dry snack is made from thin curls of seasoned beef dried until crunchy and brittle?
questions.fact: Thin biltong shavings are a favorite bar snack.

questions.q: In a potjie, in what order should ingredients traditionally be layered from bottom to top?
answers: Soft greens at bottom, meat in middle, potatoes on top
Meat and onions at bottom, hard root vegetables middle, soft greens and mushrooms on top
Vegetables at bottom, meat on top
Everything mixed into a stew before lighting coals
questions.fact: Meat browns on bottom, potatoes cook in rising steam, soft greens stay intact on top.

questions.q: What traditional Cape sweet-and-sour pickle made from green curried mangoes is served with curry and braais?
questions.fact: Mango atchar packed in spiced mustard oil.

questions.q: Which famous Scottish whiskey region is renowned for producing heavily peated, smoky single malts like Laphroaig, Ardbeg, and Lagavulin?
questions.fact: The Isle of Islay is legendary for its pungent, peaty maritime whiskies.

questions.q: What South African biscuit is baked twice so that it becomes dry, hard, and perfect for dunking into hot coffee or rooibos tea?
questions.fact: Ouma Rusks: 'Dunk a friend, dunk an Ouma!'

questions.q: What French term describes cooking meat very slowly in its own rendered fat at low temperature?
questions.fact: Duck confit is the classic example.

questions.q: Which South African craft cider brand produced in the Elgin Valley is named after the sound of apples being crushed?
questions.fact: Pioneered by Paul Cluver and Bruce Jack.

questions.q: What is the common braai etiquette regarding who is permitted to turn the meat on the grid?
answers: The guest who brought the tongs
questions.fact: Never touch another man's tongs or turn another man's meat without express permission!

questions.q: What is the highest mountain range in Southern Africa, whose name means 'Dragon Mountains' in Afrikaans?
questions.fact: uKhahlamba means 'Barrier of Spears' in Zulu; Drakensberg means Dragon Mountains.

questions.q: Which natural curved cliff face in the Northern Drakensberg rises over 1,200 meters high and stretches five kilometers long?
questions.fact: Home to the Tugela Falls, which plunge down the face of the Amphitheatre.

questions.q: What man-made canal in Egypt connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea, opening a direct maritime route to Asia?
questions.fact: Opened in November 1869, eliminating the need to sail around Africa.

questions.q: Which South African coastal road is world-famous for its cliffside curves, connecting Gordon's Bay to Rooi-Els along False Bay?
questions.fact: Clarence Drive (R44) hugs the steep sea cliffs along False Bay.

questions.q: What is the tallest building in the world today, located in Dubai, United Arab Emirates?
questions.fact: Stands 828 meters (2,717 feet) tall.

questions.q: What is the official currency of the United States of America?
questions.fact: USD ($).

questions.q: Which famous explorer led the 1519 Spanish expedition that achieved the first circumnavigation of the Earth?
questions.fact: Magellan was killed in the Philippines; Juan Sebastián Elcano completed the voyage.

questions.q: What is the capital city of Kenya?
questions.fact: Nairobi: nicknamed the 'Green City in the Sun'.

questions.q: What body of water separates the United Kingdom from the European mainland at France?
questions.fact: Connected beneath the seabed by the Channel Tunnel.

questions.q: Which South African mountain range just north of Pretoria and Johannesburg is one of the oldest geological formations on Earth?
questions.fact: The Magaliesberg is nearly 2.4 billion years old.

questions.q: What is the total overall drop height of Tugela Falls in the Drakensberg in meters?
questions.fact: 948 meters (or 983m in recent re-surveys), widely recognized as the second highest (or highest) waterfall in the world.

questions.q: How many test caps did Victor Matfield earn for the Springboks in his legendary rugby career?
questions.fact: 127 caps between 2001 and 2015.

questions.q: In what calendar year did the Suez Canal officially open for navigation?
questions.fact: Opened 17 November 1869.
